title: Building an Operational Monitoring Dashboard knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Building an Operational Monitoring Dashboard”?
options: Operational diagnosis starts by collecting the right signals: active sessions, error and slow-query logs, performance measurements, resource status, and a clear time window. Logs can contain sensitive data, so control access and retention.
It is a frontend styling feature and does not involve database behavior.
It guarantees correct output regardless of schema, permissions, or release version.
It is best handled by removing constraints and skipping error checks.
questions.answer_key: Operational diagnosis starts by collecting the right signals: active sessions, error and slow-query logs, performance measurements, resource status, and a clear time window. Logs can contain sensitive data, so control access and retention.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains: Operational diagnosis starts by collecting the right signals: active sessions, error and slow-query logs, performance measurements, resource status, and a clear time window. Logs can contain sensitive data, so control access and retention.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies “Building an Operational Monitoring Dashboard” safely?
options: Skip testing, assume every SQL engine behaves identically, and apply the change directly to production.
Concatenate untrusted input into SQL text and grant administrator privileges to every application user.
Judge success only by whether the statement returns any rows, without checking expected behavior or edge cases.
Write a read-only diagnostic checklist and identify which output or time range would confirm your hypothesis.
questions.answer_key: Write a read-only diagnostic checklist and identify which output or time range would confirm your hypothesis.
questions.explanation: Write a read-only diagnostic checklist and identify which output or time range would confirm your hypothesis. This makes the result reviewable and aligns with a controlled learning workflow.

questions.prompt: Before relying on an example for “Building an Operational Monitoring Dashboard”, what should be verified?
options: Ignore version notes and infer behavior from an unrelated database engine.
Assume a successful connection means the query and data model are correct.
Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
Run a broad production change before checking the current state.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
questions.explanation: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
